message.content:
Below are two ways to spin up a **Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Note** – “EC2” is Amazon‑AWS terminology. In Google Cloud the equivalent service is **Compute Engine**.  
>  You’ll need a project with billing enabled, the **Compute Engine API** turned on, and the **NVIDIA GPU drivers** installed after the VM boots.

---

## 1️⃣ gcloud CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1. Pick a zone that supports GPUs (e.g. us-central1-a)
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2. Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --zone=$ZONE \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: install NVIDIA drivers
```

### Optional: Install NVIDIA drivers automatically

Create a `startup.sh` script in the same directory:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Update package lists
apt-get update

# Install NVIDIA driver (the latest supported for RTX A6000)
apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535

# Reboot to activate the driver
reboot
```

Make it executable:

```bash
chmod +x startup.sh
```

When the VM starts, the script will run, install the driver, and reboot.

---

## 2️⃣ REST API (for programmatic use)

```bash
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-balanced"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "automaticRestart": true,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nreboot"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Replace `{PROJECT_ID}`, `{ZONE}`, and `{ACCESS_TOKEN}` with your actual values.  
The `startup-script` installs the NVIDIA driver and reboots the VM so the GPU is ready for use.

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| 1 | Enable **Compute Engine API** in your project. |
| 2 | Ensure **billing** is active. |
| 3 | Verify the chosen **zone** supports GPUs (`nvidia-tesla-a6000`). |
| 4 | Grant the VM’s service account the **Compute Admin** role (or at least the ability to create instances). |
| 5 | After the instance is running, SSH into it and confirm the GPU is visible: `nvidia-smi`. |

That’s all! Once the instance is up, you can SSH in and start using the RTX A6000 for your workloads.
